props.title: #Horror

sections.content: **#Horror** (2015) marks a fascinating intersection of social media anxiety and classic slasher elements. Director Tara Subkoff crafts a disturbing commentary on cyber-bullying through the lens of privileged pre-teen girls whose Instagram obsession turns deadly. The film follows similar digital-age horror themes as **Unfriended** (2014) and **Cam** (2018), but focuses more explicitly on youth culture and status-seeking behavior. Its experimental visual style, incorporating actual social media interfaces and glitch aesthetics, builds on techniques pioneered in **Searching** (2018).

sections.content: The film's commentary on wealth and privilege among American youth recalls elements of **Cruel Intentions** (1999) and **Mean Girls** (2004), but with a darker, more violent edge. Subkoff's background in fashion and art influences the film's distinctive visual style, creating a glossy veneer that gradually cracks to reveal the horror beneath. This approach echoes similar explorations of youth culture gone wrong in films like **Assassination Nation** (2018) and **Spring Breakers** (2012).

The integration of social media interfaces as narrative devices builds on techniques developed in films like **Black Mirror: Bandersnatch** (2018) and **Profile** (2018). But where those films used technology as a framework, **#Horror** makes it an active character, turning likes, comments, and filters into weapons of psychological warfare. This technique would later influence films like **Spree** (2020) and **Mainstream** (2020). SUBHEAD: Social Media Horror Evolution

sections.content: The film represents a crucial stepping stone between early internet horror films like **FearDotCom** (2002) and more sophisticated recent entries like **Host** (2020). Its emphasis on the psychological impact of constant digital connection and performance anxiety predates similar themes in **Eighth Grade** (2018) and **Social Animals** (2018), though with more explicitly horrific consequences.
